title: Gajendra Moksham
body:
Gajendra Moksham

To understand the liberation of Gajendra, one must first know the histories of the two beings whose fates were bound together in it. In the land that would one day become Puri in Odisha, there ruled a noble and devoted king named Indradyumna, whose heart overflowed with devotion to Sriman Narayana and who, it is said, built the great Jagannath Temple. So absorbed was he in his worship that when the sage Agastya once came to his court seeking hospitality, the king, lost in meditation, did not notice his arrival. Agastya, known for his fiery temper, mistook the silence for arrogance and cursed the king to be reborn as an elephant, that through such a form he might truly learn the meaning of devotion.
Elsewhere, a Gandharva named Huhu, proud of his beauty and celestial voice, once mocked the sage Devala and disturbed his penance; the angered sage cursed him to be reborn as a crocodile, to dwell in the waters until the Lord Himself should grant him release. And so two souls — a king turned elephant, a Gandharva turned crocodile — were set upon a course to meet.
Reborn as Gajendra, Indradyumna became the mighty ruler of an elephant herd upon the Mountain of Trikuta. Yet even in this new form his soul remembered, and each day he would go to a sacred lake upon the mountain, pluck a lotus from its waters with his trunk, and raise it to the sky in offering to the Lord. On one such day, as he waded into the lake, the crocodile — Huhu, bound by his curse — seized his leg and would not let go. A great struggle began, the waters churning as the elephant pulled with all his might, but the crocodile held fast. Minutes turned to hours, hours to days, and it is said the struggle wore on for a thousand years, until Gajendra's once-mighty strength began to fail him.
And then realization came. Gajendra understood that no strength, no intelligence, no kingdom, and no worldly power could save one when destiny had tightened its grip — only the Supreme could. With the last of his strength he lifted his trunk, plucked a lotus, and raised it toward the heavens, crying out to the Lord as "Aadhimoola," the primordial cause of all causes, and surrendering himself entirely at His feet. This was Sharanagati, the ultimate surrender. His cry echoed across the universe, and the Devas above, hearing it, turned away in reverence, for the title he had called upon belonged to none of them — only One could answer such a call.
And far above, in Vaikuntham, Sriman Narayana heard. He did not wait, and He did not pause; before even summoning Garuda He surged forward, and only afterward did Garuda catch up to bear Him swiftly on. By the time the Lord arrived, His Sudarshana Chakra had already sped ahead of its own accord and slain the crocodile, releasing Huhu from his curse. The Lord lifted Gajendra gently, and at that moment the elephant let go of the last thread binding him to the world; his soul, now purified, merged into the divine radiance, and he was granted liberation. It is said that the lotus which remained in the Lord's hand was the very one Gajendra had offered that day. Thus the tale teaches that no strength or wisdom or wealth can save one when destiny strikes — the Lord does not measure devotion by status, nor wait for grand ritual; the moment His devotee truly calls, He comes.
